Let \(A\) be the set of chess players with a rating greater than 1500, \(B\) be the set of chess players with a rating greater than 1800, and \(C\) be the set of chess players with a rating greater than 2100. Draw a Venn diagram to represent this situation. Which description is correct?
options: Three circles one inside the other: \(C\) inside \(B\) inside \(A\), all inside the universal set
Three overlapping circles with a common region
Three separate circles that do not touch
Two overlapping circles \(A\) and \(B\) with \(C\) outside both
questions.hint: Ask: if a player is in \(C\) (rating over 2100), must they ALSO be in \(B\) and \(A\)? A rating over 2100 is also over 1800 and over 1500.

steps.explain: Rating over 2100 implies rating over 1800.

questions.stem: Consider the set of points on the line segment \([0,1]\). If you remove the middle third but leave the end points, the new set is \(\left[0,\dfrac{1}{3}\right]\cup\left[\dfrac{2}{3},1\right]\). If you now remove the middle third from each of these line segments but leave the end points, and repeat this process forever, you are left with a special set, called the Cantor set. Show that the Cantor set is an infinite set. (Hint: find an infinite subset.)

So the set \(\left\{\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{1}{9},\dfrac{1}{27},\ldots\right\}\) is a subset of the Cantor set, and it has infinitely many members (one for each \(n=1,2,3,\ldots\)).
A set containing an infinite subset is infinite. Hence the Cantor set is infinite.  ∎
